newsitem.title: USA: Singer Brown won't face Florida assault charge.
newsitem.headline: Singer Brown won't face Florida assault charge.

text.p: Prosecutors have ruled out legal action against singer Bobby Brown for his alleged role in the 1995 beating of a Chicago man at Disney World, Brown's attorney said Wednesday.

Prosecutors dropped aggravated assault charges against Brown, husband of pop diva Whitney Houston, last November after he reached an out-of-court settlement with the victim, who refused to testify against Brown once he was paid.
But prosecutor Robert Welch said at the time there was a "very, very strong possibility" that he would re-file the charges against Brown and two members of his entourage.
Brown's criminal defence attorney, Robert Buanauro, said Wednesday that prosecutors had now ruled that out.
"The state attorney's office decided it wasn't in the best interest of the citizens of Florida to try to force the alleged victim to testify against his will," Buanauro said.
Welch did not return a phone call seeking comment Wednesday.

Charges against Brown's publicist, Travis Boyce, also were dropped. Brown's bodyguard, Gary Smith, entered a no contest plea to a battery charge last month and paid a fine but received no jail time and adjudication was withheld, Buanauro said.
Brown, 27, was set to go on trial in November when he reached an 11th-hour settlement with Neil Kelly, 38. Brown could have been sentenced to three years in prison if found guilty.
Brown, who had a top 10 hit with "Don't Be Cruel," and his two companions were arrested in April 1995 while staying at a luxury Disney World resort.
Police said Kelly was beaten and stomped on, even after losing consciousness. Kelly's partially severed ear was reattached at a local hospital.
Police determined that Brown and Kelly began to argue after Kelly made advances to a woman socializing with Brown.

Kelly initially demanded $6.6 million to settle the case. He later dropped his demand to $2.5 million. Although Brown's lawyers would not say what he paid, published reports put the amount at less than $100,000.
"This thing has been about money from the start," Buanauro said. "These people were minding their own business before Mr. Kelly entered the scene."
